rv.q: Even if the play repeats the expected beats, it at least does so with humor and gets in and out quickly.

Sometimes, however, it doesn’t pour rain. What’s poured instead is scotch, bourbon, rum, and beer. Only days ago, the musicalized Days of Wine and Roses , in which Kirsten Arnesen and Joe Clay indulge in an alcoholic maelstrom, opened.
It’s a compelling revelation in a play that’s both admirable and tonally jarring.

cn.t: Critics find "The White Chip" tonally uneven, with its sitcom-like cheerfulness undercutting the serious subject matter of addiction and recovery despite an eager central performance.
